questions.question: How does the brightness of two bulbs connected in parallel compare to the same two bulbs connected in series when powered by the same battery?
options: The bulbs in parallel are brighter than those in series.
The bulbs in series are brighter than those in parallel.
The bulbs in parallel are dimmer than those in series.
The bulbs in both circuit types have the exact same brightness.

questions.question: If you connect two bulbs in parallel instead of in series to the same battery, what happens to the total current flowing from the battery?
options: The current is smaller through the parallel circuit than the series circuit.
The current is bigger through the parallel circuit than the series circuit.
The current remains exactly the same in both circuits.
No current flows at all in the parallel circuit.

questions.question: If you set up two circuits using identical batteries—one with two bulbs in series and another with two bulbs in parallel—which battery will run out of energy faster?
options: The battery in the series circuit will run out faster.
The battery in the parallel circuit will run out faster.
Both batteries will run out of energy at exactly the same time.
Neither battery will run out of energy because the bulbs are identical.

questions.question: What does an ammeter measure, and in what unit?
options: It measures voltage in volts (V).
It measures current in amps (A).
It measures resistance in ohms (Ω).
It measures power in watts (W).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes electrical resistance?
options: A measure of how easily electrons can pass through a vacuum.
A measure of how difficult it is for an electric current to flow.
The speed at which voltage travels around a closed loop.
The rate at which energy is transferred to a battery.

questions.question: What is the standard unit of measurement for electrical resistance?
options: Amps (A)
Volts (V)
Ohms (Ω)
Watts (W)

questions.question: How does the length of a wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: The longer the wire, the smaller its resistance.
The longer the wire, the greater its resistance.
The length of the wire does not affect its resistance.
A longer wire has zero resistance.

questions.question: If the length of a specific uniform wire is doubled, what happens to its resistance?
options: Its resistance is halved.
Its resistance is doubled.
Its resistance is quartered.
Its resistance remains exactly the same.

questions.question: Which mathematical relationship correctly describes the connection between the resistance of a uniform wire and its length?
options: The resistance of a wire is proportional to its length.
The resistance of a wire is inversely proportional to its length.
The resistance of a wire is equal to its length squared.
There is no mathematical relationship between resistance and length.

questions.question: In electrical systems, what does "power" measure?
options: The total electrical charge stored within a cell or battery.
The amount of energy used by or supplied to a device in one second.
The total resistance of a circuit over a period of one hour.
The push that moves electrons through a single component.

questions.question: What is the standard unit of measurement for electrical power?
options: Volts (V)
Watts (W)
Ohms (Ω)
Amps (A)

questions.question: How do you calculate the electrical energy used by a device in kilowatt-hours (kWh)?
options: Divide the power in kilowatts (kW) by the time in hours (h).
Multiply the power in kilowatts (kW) by the time in hours (h).
Multiply the current in amps (A) by the resistance in ohms (Ω).
Add the power in kilowatts (kW) to the time in hours (h).

questions.question: When looking at a household electricity bill, what is "1 unit of energy" equal to?
options: 1 watt (W)
1 kilowatt-hour (kWh)
1 amp-hour (Ah)
1 volt per second (V/s)

questions.question: Which of the following is the definition of a parallel circuit?
options: A circuit containing only a single continuous loop from one end of a battery to the other.
A circuit with more than one complete loop, from one end of a battery to the other end.
A circuit where components are connected one after another in a single line.
A circuit that does not require a cell or battery to allow current to flow.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, how does the current flowing through each individual branch relate to the total current through the battery?
options: The current through each branch is always equal to the total current through the battery.
The current through each branch adds up to the total current through the battery.
The current through each branch is subtracted from the total battery current.
The total current through the battery is divided by the square of the number of branches.

questions.question: How does the thickness of a wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: The thicker the wire, the greater its resistance.
The thicker the wire, the smaller its resistance.
The thickness of a wire has no effect on its resistance.
A thicker wire always has infinite resistance.

questions.question: If you double the cross-sectional area of a wire, what happens to its resistance?
options: Its resistance doubles.
Its resistance halves.
Its resistance quadruples.
Its resistance remains unchanged.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, how does the voltage across each branch compare to the voltage across the power source?
options: The voltage across each branch is halved.
The voltage across each branch is the same as the voltage across the cell or battery.
The voltage across each branch adds up to the total voltage of the cell or battery.
The voltage across each branch is always zero volts.
